# Simulation: Similar Concepts

This branch supports comparative review of concepts that sound similar but differ in state ownership, gates, effects, parameters, or user-facing purpose. It does not delete concepts automatically.

| Concept pair | Distinction | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACCR vs ALLOY | Both use merge infrastructure; ACCR is overlap/fusion behavior while ALLOY targets different-species composite mixing. | [src/physics/mergePhysics.js](../../../src/physics/mergePhysics.js); [src/state/lawHelpPatches.js](../../../src/state/lawHelpPatches.js) |
| BOND vs ADHESION | BOND is persistent valence structure; ADHESION is bounded near-contact attraction and does not merge mass. | [src/physics/laws.js](../../../src/physics/laws.js); [src/physics/lawgroups/mechanicsLaws.js](../../../src/physics/lawgroups/mechanicsLaws.js) |
| FIELD law vs field medium | The law is a toggleable drift/force concept; the medium is a stateful grid sampled by the solver. | [src/constants.js](../../../src/constants.js); [src/physics/fields.js](../../../src/physics/fields.js) |
| HORIZON vs SINGULARITY | HORIZON is a pairwise boundary effect; SINGULARITY includes supermassive pull and absorption behavior. | [src/physics/lawgroups/physicsLaws.js](../../../src/physics/lawgroups/physicsLaws.js); [src/physics/solver.js](../../../src/physics/solver.js) |
| ANTIMATTER vs HYPERPLANE | ANTIMATTER is matter interaction/annihilation; HYPERPLANE is quantum position/space transformation. | [src/physics/lawgroups/quantumLaws.js](../../../src/physics/lawgroups/quantumLaws.js); [src/state/exoticMatter.js](../../../src/state/exoticMatter.js) |
| INERTIA vs MASS_INERTIA | INERTIA is slate Mechanics behavior; MASS_INERTIA is the Physics addition and must not share a bit. | [src/physics/lawgroups/mechanicsLaws.js](../../../src/physics/lawgroups/mechanicsLaws.js); [src/physics/lawgroups/physicsLaws.js](../../../src/physics/lawgroups/physicsLaws.js) |

A concept is truly redundant only when state mutation, gate, effect, parameters, and user-facing purpose are materially identical and no persistence, UI, audit, or compatibility contract depends on the distinction.
